#3761. Hollow Knight: Silksong devs announce a livestream for Friday, promise updates on the hotly-anticipated Sea of Sorrow DLC

Hollow Knight: Silksong developer Team Cherry has announced it will host a 'Cherry Time Special Presentation' on 27th November, bringing more information to light about the game's first big DLC offering, Sea of Sorrows. We know that the free update will be nautically-themed - hence the eponymous 'sea' - and will feature new bosses, areas and so on, but other than that, information about what's coming is vague.

But it seems that's not all; as well as more information about the mysterious update to the hit Metroidvania game, the studio has also announced "a bunch" of other "exciting announcements." Curious.

The Cherry Time Special Presentation will kick off at 7am PT / 10am ET / 3pm GMT / 4pm CEST. I'll embed the video below, so check back here at the time if you need a bookmark.

Recently, and more than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong finally began arriving on players' doorsteps. Whilst these editions contained mostly expected information, there was an unforeseen mention of "free content packs" that would be arriving alongside the Sea of Sorrow DLC. Will we hear more about these as part of this new showcase? We don't have too long to find out.

It seems likely, though. "The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet read in the physical editions. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with new friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!" Team Cherry has repeatedly confirmed plans for post-launch Silksong support, but other than this upcoming DLC, we don't really know what that entails.

Additionally, Sea of Sorrow's original release window was a vague 2026 - will we see it shadowdrop as part of this stream? Stranger things have happened, especially in the world of Hollow Knight…

#3758. "Clearly not everything has gone well" during Fable's lengthy creation, says Playground boss, but the "original vision" remains intact despite taking cues from other RPGs

"Looking only to the original Fable trilogy for inspiration would leave us lacking"

The Fable reboot is finally set to kick the release chicken (I'm not sure that's an established phrase anywhere in the world, but roll with it) early next year, following a not small amount of time in development and multiple delays. Despite that long time in the oven having made it necessary to look beyond just the series' classic entries for RPG inspiration, Playground Games' Fable general manager has said the team's "original vision" of what a Fable game needs to be hasn't changed.

I say this with some pride – tempered against the fact that this has been obviously an enormously long development, so clearly not everything has gone well – but I would say that our original vision of what Fable needs to be has remained unchanged," Ralph Fulton, one of Playground's co-founders, told our suit-wearing siblings at GIBiz.

"There are many reasons that this game development has been long," he added. "It's a new team, it's a new genre, a new franchise, new technology – although we're building in an engine that we know well. It's also because a Fable game must have a great story with memorable characters and high-stakes drama, and also it needs to be funny and to have that British wit infused throughout it. Then there's combat, the quest structure, and the world of Albion and its people, and the simulations that underpin it. You'd be nuts to take on all of that in the first project, and yet here we are."

Fulton went on to note that despite that, Playground have worked to ensure their game's scope hasn't grown ever wider as they've made it. One call made early on with the social and economic simming that goes with the likes of landlording and being a dick to entire villages was that the studio "would only model first and second degree ripple effects", due to feeling that "players would only notice or we could only communicate the consequences up to the second degree". That makes sense, not every game can or should be a strategy game like Civ, wherein seeing your actions cause or influence a thousand different tidal waves over time is part of the central appeal. Not every game also has the budget of a GTA 6, which works deep simulation mechanics into a crime adventure, but feels like an exception to the rules even compared to Xbox-backed games like Fable.

On the other hand, Fulton did make clear that Playground have looked beyond the original entries in the series for RPG inspiration, fearing their game might be left behind if not. "Principally, technology has advanced," he said when asked what's changed while the game's been in the works. "In 2015, The Witcher 3 redefined what an open-world action RPG looks like and became the gold standard. And after that bar was raised, the Assassin's Creed franchise changed into this more modern iteration with Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla, and became like a quasi-RPG.

"All of these games continue to reset player expectations, which means I think looking only to the original Fable trilogy for inspiration would leave us lacking in terms of what the modern audience, the modern marketplace, expects."

We've already seen some of the ways in which the reboot diverges from its older forebears. As far as I'm concerned, albeit as someone with only a brief dalliance in the classic Fables, such tweaks could go either way. It is interesting to see Assassin's Creed mentioned alongside The Witcher 3 as having changed the RPG game. A game like Baldur's Gate 3 or even Starfield would strike me as a more obvious candidate to point to, so the AC mention might offer some indiction of the direction Playground have taken with their design.

Fable is, of course, being backed by Microsoft. The company are subject to an ongoing boycott by the BDS movement and have inflicted significant layoffs on their Xbox studios this year. As for whether the latter upheaval has affected Playground or Xbox's backing of Fable, Fulton offered a rather nothing answer here about Forza Horizon being good for the studio and the importance of keeping everyone internally in the loop as to how work on the game's going.

#3757. World of Warcraft: Forever's best new enchantment has been quietly changed, leaving some casters on the back foot

As World of Warcraft: Forever players dived into the game, they quickly discovered a specific weapon enchant that took area of effect spells to a whole other level. Sadly, with a sudden hotfix last night, this particular use case for the enchant has been removed.

The enchantment in question was Revelation - a new addition to the game included as part of the new trade good reputations. What it does is simple: when you fail to deal a critical strike with a spell, the next spell hit is guaranteed to do so. What made this particularly powerful is that the buff also worked with continuous area of effect spells, meaning an early instance of the spell not crit-ing would result in the remaining damage hits all dealing critical damage.

So for example, let's say you're a druid casting the Hurricane spell. This is a channel spell with a total of 10 seconds of cast time. Every second, it deals damage. If the first instance of damage at the one second mark doesn't crit, the remaining nine instances of damage would all crit. This resulted in absurd amounts of damage, and made players of druids, warlocks, and mages very happy.

While strong enchantments are often pricey, this was notably cheap, due to the low-cost of resources used to create it and the low requirements to learn it. As such, people were spending a handful of gold for an early game enchantment that was being actively used all the way into the end game.

It was admittedly a tad too strong, and the effect triggered on AOE spells was almost certainly an unintended effect of the enchantment. Last night, the fun came to an end. Now, the effect is used up as intended in long-casted spells. So going back to the example given, if the first instance of damage on Hurricane doesn't crit, then the second one still will. However, this will use up the effect, and the third instance of damage will revert to regular ol' damage numbers. It also seems as though it Revelation can't trigger more than once during a single channeled spell.

This is the latest in a string of ongoing quickfire bug fixes and game adjustments being made to World of Warcraft: Forever. The devs have been continuously updating the game in an attempt to curb certain gold farms, following the discovery of a particularly lucrative Blackmaw Hold gold exploit. The dev team has expressed some interesting ideas for the game longterm, including a desire to kill best-in-slot gear.

Character customization in GTA has never been so good, and you even have two characters to fit this time around, meaning there are more choices than ever when picking Jason and Lucia's GTA 6 outfits, tattoos, and hairstyles.

You may have already seen just a few of the countless variants for Lucia's hair doing the rounds on socials, but since different shops and stylists offer different options, it's not always easy to find what you're after. That's where we come in. This is our growing list of our favorite GTA 6 outfits, including exactly where to pick them up for yourself, so make sure you have enough cash to spend by checking out our guide to the best ways to get money fast in GTA 6, then go shopping.

The best hairstyles and colors for Lucia can usually be found in the Signature section at specific stylists, as this is where unique styles can be found that you can't just find everywhere.

Check out these styles and where to get them below:

You've probably seen this Spiky Twin Buns style online as it seems to be the crowd-favorite Lucia style, and it can be found in the Signature section at Clip & Fade in Stockyard, Vice City. While this looks great with a solid hair color, I personally love this look with the pink color, as the contrast between Lucia's warm brunette roots and the bright pink spiky buns looks super cool. You can get this pink ombre dye at Pearl Hair Salon in Port Gellhorn.

If you prefer something a bit more natural and cultural, then give these gorgeous Goddess Box Braids a go - they're a very popular style right now. While I'd usually opt for a pop of color in Lucia's hair (to counter all that black I've got her wearing), this style best suits a nice warm brunette. You can get this in a few places, but I'd recommend Crosstown Cutz in, well, Crosstown, Vice City.

For something a little more sophisticated, try out this slicked back bun and forehead curl look with a platinum blonde or a deep, dark brown. This might be a style you want to try out for a night on the town rather than a bank heist or a day car jacking, but each to their own. Head to the stylist at Crosstown Cutz in Vice City to try it out.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

My personal favorite hairstyle for Lucia, though, is this wavy high ponytail and braids look that you can also get from Clip & Fade (can you figure out my top salon pick, yet?). Not only does it looks absolutely amazing on our female protagonist, but it shows off the incredible GTA 6 hair physics better than any other hairstyle I've seen yet.

While this style suits any color, I particularly think it looks great in a bright shade, so go for this Intense Red, again available at Clip & Fade, or the pink from above.

It's very worth noticing the cool detail that Lucia's make-up smudges if she stays up too long without getting it touched up. This is more obvious in cut scenes than just exploring surroundings, so make sure you've got the best make-up on before starting a new mission.

To make Lucia's make up stand out, it's worth picking something with a bright lip or bold eye. This Classic Vinewood look checks that first box with a super glossy red lip and a subtle smokey eye. Get it at Hair by Clair in Capri.

This one's a bit subtler on first glance, but on closer inspection, you'll see a cute smattering of gold stars lining Lucia's eyes, leading to this look's name: Celestial. What first drew me to this looks, though, was the gorgeous coral lipstick, and if you like it too, you can get it at Salon Belle in Rockridge.

Finally, this strong, smoky, retro look perfect compliments Lucia's attitude and many of her best outfits. I particularly love the dark liner - it's time that look came back. You can also find this look at Salon Belle in Rockridge.

My favorite nail art options for Lucia are:

Honestly, my favorite nails for Lucia are the retro Glossy Red Nails that can be picked up anywhere, but only with the Vintage Vice City Pack. This was a pre-order bonus, so you might already have it, but you can purchase the pack separately if not. With the pack, you can get this set anywhere that does nails, but you'll need to tab across to the 'Special Nails' menu.

If you don't have the Vintage Vice City pack and don't want to fork out real-life cash for a set of virtual nails, then I also love this long tortoiseshell set you can get from Salon Belle in Rockridge. It's tricky to find this salon, as it's located inside a residential block, but once you do, you can get these nails in long or short variants, as well as a load of other unique hair and nail designs.

These are my top picks for Jason's hair and facial hair in GTA 6:

Honestly, Jason's standard haircuts are some of his best, and you can get those at any salon. Personally, I switch between this mid-length wavy slick back style and the long slick back style. You can always tweak the color to make it a bit more interesting, for example with a dusty blue bye from Pearl Hair Salon in Port Gellhorn or a bright pink or green from Clip & Fade.

Some good signature styles can be found for Jason, though, and this Short Slick Back look at Hair by Clair in Capri is among them, as one of the nicer shorter styles I've seen.

Look, sometimes, you may as well fit in with the locals, and there's no better way of doing that in the Port Gellhorn area than with a good old mullet. Whether or not you want to change it up by the time you get to Vice City is up to you, but you'll find this iconic style at Pearl Hair Salon in south Port Gellhorn.

Selecting and showcasing the best outfits for Lucia is a near impossible task, honestly, as there are just so many options out there. However, I've listed a few of my personal favorites below to give a brief snapshot of what's on offer and what each store stocks.

For a cool, casual day-to-night outfit, I just love this look on Lucia. These pants are my absolute go-to since they look great paired with any bodysuit or crop top (I'm also a big fan of the red high-neck bodysuit from location). However, you're not going to get away with an underboob crop top quite this short in real life without constant anxiety of a wardrobe malfunction, so I figure why not wear one when you know it's not going anywhere. You could always put something over the top until it's time to hit clubs if you're feel self-conscious.

Okay, I like wearing black, and that seems to be a trait I'm forcing onto Lucia, too, but that doesn't mean you have to. The bodysuit I've paired with the skirt above only comes in a black, but there are other similar one-pieces available in red, purple, and even leopard print, if that's your thing. Check them out at the back of Ferruccio Tucci stores.

Similarly, this gorgeous thigh-split skirt comes in other colors too, making them look more like beach wear, while this soft black can comfortably be worn in any environment. Sadly, I can't remember where I picked the skirt up, but as soon as I find it again, I'll update you here.

This one again is part of the Vintage Vice City pack, but how could I not include it as one of Lucia's best looks. It's a no-brainer - Lucia looks great alongside Jason in his equivalent fit, and they both work it particularly well against a classic GTA 6 car like the Dundreary Chino. Just get that beaut kitted out at your local mod shop, and you'll be ready to ride around Leonida in style.

Provided you've got the Vintage Vice City pack, you can unlock this look at any clothing retailer marked with a yellow price tag. You'll have to equip the hair and make-up separately, but you can do both at most hair salons.

Finally, you can't go wrong with a cute grungy outfit for Lucia, and this pair of baggy jeans from Mid is among the easiest pieces to team with any of her cute top options. One of my favorites, though, is this bandana top from Aline's Thrift Store in La Perle. Finally, get Lucia a pair of comfy Vans-style slip-ons from Mid to finish of the look.

As with Lucia, there are far too many options to choose from, so here's just a few options to inspire and to give an example of what different stores have to offer.

Slater are denim specialists, and you'll even be able to pick up this ready-made outfit in their stores across Leonida. It's a classic American look, and if you want to go all Justin and Britney on us, you can pick up a matching denim look for Lucia while you're there.

Unlike with Lucia, I like to put a bit more color into Jason's clothes, and I love this combo that just screams classic Floridian - I mean Leonidian - smart casual. You'll be able to pick up the knit shirt from the This That chain of stores, while the green pants can be found in any of the Nola branches across Vice City. Both offer a variety of smart-casual garments for both Jason and Lucia. I'm still not sold on this particular pair of shoes, though, so have a browse for a pair you like. Footwear can be found in both clothes stores and dedicated shoe shops, so there's plenty of choice.

There's nothing quite like rocking up to a bank robbery looking this suave - no one's expecting you to pull out a pistol in an outfit like this. You can pick up a suit for both Jason and Lucia at Ferruccio Tucci formalwear stores across the map, though Lucia's don't look as good. Instead, browse the bodysuits for her while you're here.

Finally, we've gone for a casual rocker look, mainly thanks to this t-shirt and jacket found at Aline's Thrift Store in La Perle. Team them with some jeans and either some boots or a pair of Vans knock offs from Mid, then complete the look with headphones from any local tech shop.

If you're working on keeping your GTA 6 relationship status high, then you might want to consider getting matching tattoos with your beau. There aren't many of these, and one is locked behind a special side quest, but I can't get enough of this 'In this Life...' '...and the next' pair. This is another one I've had equipped for a while and can't quite remember where I got it, but I'm looking, and I'll update you here when I find it.

We've got loads more GTA 6 guides, so check them out if you're looking for more help as you explore Leonida.

#3755. Ubisoft now require their devs to explain why they aren't using genAI in game pitches, claims report, though the Assassin's Creed publishers deny they're mandating it

Company are all in on the tech, it's claimed

Ubisoft, they of the recently revealed generative AI-focused game studio Motherbrain, have denied they're forcing new games being pitched by their developers to integrate use of genAI as a rule. The publishers' statement comes in the wake of a report claiming that Ubisoft devs with pitches that don't use genAI are required to explain in detail why they've decided it isn't suitable for the game being outlined.

The report from Vertical Slice cited anonymous Ubisoft staff as having said that the publishers' game pitching process now requires devs to either outline how they'll use generative AI to speed up production, or offer a specific justification as to why the tech isn't being used.

Ubisoft management reportedly revealed the change during a presentation to staff, with one source telling Vertical Slice that the company are all in on generative AI. They cited an "attitude shift" among Ubisoft management as having left workers feeling "cornered by generative AI all the time", but made clear Ubisoft haven't brought in a blanket mandate forcing devs to use genAI no matter what.

Ubisoft have emphasised the latter in a statement subsequently issued to Vertical Slice. "We encourage our teams to explore where AI can be useful and bring value to their work," the company wrote. "This doesn’t mean that projects are required to use generative AI. Teams need to determine whether, and how, these technologies make sense for the game they want to make and the experience they want to create for players."

Ubisoft have been keen on experimenting with genAI in game development for a little while - something essentially set in stone by the establishing of Motherbrain as a proper division where the company can work on the likes of the "first playable generative AI experience" they were shouting about earlier this year. That move came in a year Ubisoft have spent vast swaths of laying off staff and closing studios, as part of a restructuring they kicked off with a barrage of cancellations in January.

Most recently, those cuts hit 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on a list of other affected subsidiaries that I'm very much getting tired of wheeling out whenever Ubisoft inevitably insist on adding to it.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

#3754. Why did Rockstar Games make empathy a key mechanic in GTA 6? "Because it's fun" says head of development Rob Nelson

That, and parts of RDR2 became "too hard to ignore or walk away from".

There's been plenty of chatter about Grand Theft Auto 6's 'honour system', so to speak, implemented here via what the game calls your Criminal Profile.

Our own Dom just wrote that they prefer to turn its notifications off, for instance, in favour of fully soaking into the immersion. Personally I quite like the pop-ups - I find the act of figuring out systems and how they're manipulated almost as fun as the games they're a part of. And pop-ups or no, the fact that GTA 6 can arguably be portrayed as 'rewarding' empathy and 'discouraging' the series' famous rampages of mass violence has sparked a fair bit of debate.

Some of that is genuinely interesting - I'm dubious as to whether that's really what this system is doing, for a start. Is it incentivising and disincentivising certain in-game behaviour, or just putting a label on it? And then, actually: does the act of labelling "psycho" behaviour alone actually become a disincentivising factor in itself?

Either way, until now Rockstar hasn't said a great deal about why, exactly, this system - seen by some as one that builds empathy into GTA's chaotic world - was implemented in the first place. But during an interview I had with Rob Nelson, Rockstar Games' head of development, just before GTA 6's launch earlier this month, a little more on that came to light.

A little context is necessary here: Nelson's response was actually following a question I had about the overall approach to design that Rockstar took, and how its wider themes and intentions came about. As a part of that, he turned to this system - and how, in a way, it exists here because of the work the studio simply didn't want to leave behind after Red Dead Redemption 2.

Nelson explained that this all began when the team was in the early phase of exploring what type of game GTA 6 would be, in 2015 and 2016, while much of the studio was still working full-tilt on RDR2 - a game which itself didn't release until late 2018. The team was looking to "build up the sophistication of the NPC population, and also allow for more player choice than we had [before], and more options in terms of the way you interact with the world beyond just violence," Nelson told me.

The idea would be that "it's still a world of violence - but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money." Ideas that were "simple things" in principle, he said, "but they create a lot more work in terms of development of the sophistication of the systems."

Then, as systems were gradually implemented, it became a question of "trying to marry up what you're doing in the open world with who we're saying you are in the narrative - more than we had, I would say, previously, in Red Dead 2." It's here where the system now referred to as the Criminal Profile started to form.

The thinking turned to "the nature of 'honour', which wasn't always a part of it" with Red Dead Redemption 2, Nelson continued, "but became part of it as we were working on this story and finding that the 'redemption arc' didn't feel so good when it was foisted upon you - and feelings that we had playing Red Dead sort of early on." (Those feelings, primarily, were around getting you to invest in a gang led by Dutch Van der Linde, who was fundamentally unlikable from the off - or plain "crazy", as Nelson put it. The implementation of more player choices and agency was part of Rockstar's way to build investment in Arthur, even as he followed Dutch.)

That meant moving the choices away from key story moments, where many games tend to put them. Instead, Rockstar built a system that ran alongside the story via smaller, moment-to-moment choices you might make. "We tried to take all of those off the main flow and make them optional. So again, they're a choice."

"Usually they involve some form of slight sacrifice or more effort on the part of the player," he added. The hope, then, was that you as a player would both "feel something", and ultimately also feel "you got the outcome that you deserved."

That was the initial thinking behind this kind of system as a whole. Coming to GTA 6, it then combined with a wider desire to "evolve" Grand Theft Auto as both the team's storytelling and the available technology matured. "You're thinking about story and character set, but we're also thinking about what we want to do with GTA as a series, and how you want to evolve it," Nelson said.

"I think as the resolution goes up, it sort of asks different new questions," he continued. "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics. So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun."

"It's fun for some people like myself to just sort of role-play in the world, and be in the world, and restraint becomes something you hadn't thought about," he continued. That tied back into the more sophisticated NPCs and reactions the team were making.

"If you think about the NPCs, even back to [GTA] 5, you would draw a weapon - first of all, they didn't react if you drew an invisible shotgun out of nowhere, or a rocket launcher," he said. "They don't react unless you aim it, and then they flee in terror, and you're just sort of this demigod stomping through the world, you know? And that's fun, but for how long?

"The team then started thinking of ways to build a bit more sustained enjoyment from it. "What if you can't do that?" Nelson continued. What if, instead of whipping an RPG out of nowhere, "you have to call your car. You have to pop a car trunk and get it, and now I'm walking, and now people are noticing, but they're sort of sidling away, and it's more believable. And then they're still fleeing in terror, but then there's people who also have guns, and they're shooting at you, or you try to hold somebody up and they pull a gun, or they grab it, and then you have to deal with them.

"And then, he continued, "you choose. You're trying to jack somebody off a motorcycle, and they pull a gun on you, and you have to blow their head off and it's like, 'You shouldn't have made me do that!' And so then it has more meaning, and it's more funny in a way when it's a little bit more pointed. And you can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks and then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'"

That Irredeemable profile level, for what it's worth, was another element born of Red Dead Redemption 2. "We had that with Red Dead, where people would sort of have low honour, and then 'greet' their way back up to high honour. And so this was an attempt of sorts of [making something] for people that just want to go crazy and almost opt out of the system. They can opt out of it - and you can also turn off the notifications in the system."

It's notable, in fact, just how interlinked the thinking was with GTA 6 and Red Dead Redemption 2. As Nelson put it at one point: "There was maybe more emotional resonance in the story of RDR2 than we had had, certainly in a GTA before. So we liked that idea." What Rockstar did with GTA 6 was then in a way a natural next step. "We didn't necessarily come to GTA 6 going: 'We must have emotional resonance,' but all of those things combine. It's more that those systems and that element of player choice and agency, and the way that affected the narrative, was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from."

We'll have much more like this from our interview with Nelson very soon, so do look out for that on Eurogamer over the coming days. In the meantime, we've a handy guide explaining exactly how GTA 6's Criminal Profile system works and how to change, raise, or lower that profile if you're in need of a deep dive into how it all really works.

I've lost count of how many times I've settled down to play a brand-new game on Steam, only to be smacked in the face with a giant popup telling me to "Grab a controller and kick back!" instead of using my humble mouse and keyboard.

Thankfully for me I live in a multi-platform household, meaning a controller is never far out of reach. But I've also got staunch PC pals without a pad to pick up and who, rightly enough, don't want to fork out the kinda cash that PlayStation's DualSense or the Xbox controller require.

But I'm a firm believer that a good controller is a must-have tool in a PC gamer's repertoire these days, and we needn't immediately seek out the big names when it comes to a comfortable, robust gamepad. Tons of budget-friendly options have popped up on the market over the years, and while some of them are admittedly pretty naff there are also a bunch of great controllers that won't break the bank.

In fact, I've got three of 'em for under $25 for you right here. That's a third of the price of a DualSense controller! While they don't come with fancy haptics and adaptive triggers, they do offer stick-drift resistant, low-latency gaming. Which, as fun as the bells as whistles can be, are really the most important bits.

A new and improved version of the original Nova Lite, the Nova Lite 2 has Hall effect everything, 1000 Hz polling, and trigger locks. It even has a mechanical D-pad, which is absurd for the money, really.

Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect

Out of the three choices, our pad professional James Bentley tells me he likes the GameSir Nova Lite 2 the best, currently going for $23 at Walmart. It boasts comfort, decent polling, and Hall effect—so much better protection against that pesky stick drift. It's also got our highest review score out of the bunch thanks to its affordability, mechanical d-pad, and choice of 2.4Ghz and Bluetooth.

It's not got great grip, however, and its budget is felt in the less-than-stellar plastic and rather simple software. But for the price you're paying? It's a great, basic choice for those who only need to reach for a controller occasionally.

We've already raved about Hall effect joysticks and how they spell the end for the dreaded stick drift. In this wireless gaming controller, they're a welcome feature, but this handful of gaming hardware packs a few quirky surprises too. For instance, there are extra bumper buttons.

Key specs: Hall effect sticks, triggers | 2.4G wireless | 19 h battery

Price check: Best Buy $21.99 (Black) | Walmart $29.99 (Purple)

But if you're someone who's accustomed to the likes of the Switch Pro controller, you might find the 8BitDo Ultimate 2C a better fit, currently going for $20 at Amazon. It's got a pretty similar shape, and also sports those beloved Hall effect joysticks. It does have a little bit of a mushy d-pad but hey, look at that lovely colourway!

Finally, if you're looking to spend as little as possible, the GameSir Nova Lite comes in as the cheapest option at a mere $18. It's got less mappable buttons than its successor thanks to no back paddles, and is overall a downgrade. For the extra four bucks I'd personally just go for the newer version, but if you're really looking to really squeeze every cent, it's certainly an option worth considering.

It's incredible to think you can spend so little and get a stick drift-resistant wireless controller that doesn't completely suck. Luckily for the GameSir Nova Lite, it does all of the above and manages to feel good and light in the hands, too.

Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect

#3750. An apology from RPS

Yesterday I made a significant error in judgement. In writing an apology to our readers, I made a target of one of our writers and I won't be able to undo that. What I can try to do is apologise to that writer, who I'm addressing now.

My failures towards you were several. Firstly, in not explaining that we are able to step in by replying to and moderating comments when a discussion is becoming heated or aggressive, I never made it clear there were protections available to you that you weren't receiving.

Secondly, for mentioning you at all in the apology. While I hoped to make it clear to readers we wouldn't disrespect them in future, I laid the blame for that on your feet in public. The responsibility of an editor is to protect their writers, and I failed you profoundly.

Thirdly, that I didn't speak to you ahead of the post. As far as you were concerned the matter was settled, and I then put it in public without any warning.

Fourth, while we often talk of RPS being a collection of different writers with different viewpoints, where no one member of the team has the definitive view on a subject, this creates a vacuum for our contributors to operate in. This means new writers have very little direction when it comes to how they approach any topic and the response their work may receive. Again, any failings here are ultimately my responsibility.

Finally, this failure is all the more significant because it has happened across lines of gender privilege. RPS has a full-time staff of cisgender men, which inevitably gives rise to bias and ignorance we must actively confront, while we work towards being in a position to address our lack of gender diversity, beyond commissioning the occasional marginalised freelance writer. Non-cisgender writers are both much more exposed to abuse and much less favoured in terms of steady work. As such, a public rebuke from your own editor is far more damaging than it would be if the freelancer were a cisgender man. On this count, I have been extremely thoughtless in ways that would likely not have been the case when this site had a majority female editorship.

Ashley, I am deeply sorry that I let you down in these ways.

Affordable wired gaming headsets that work on the Switch

If you want your Nintendo Switch 2 to sound as good as possible, you won't dream of using the handheld's built-in stereo speakers, and will pick up a headset to use with the system. It won't cost you much to do so, with Black Friday deals cutting cost on gaming-designed headphones.

There are loads of Black Friday gaming headset deals at Currys, with the best reducing models down to lovely tempting prices. Some are discounted to below £50, which means they're cheaper than the cost of a Switch 2 game. They're all wired models, as cable-toting tech is generally cheaper, which means these options still offer some impressive specs despite the low price. In particular there are four headsets below this price threshold which work on the Switch 2, and you can find them below, ordered from cheapest to priciest.

This wired Logitech gaming headset is over 50% off, despite its specs. It offers 7.1 sound, and is certified as a DTS Headphone:X headphone. It's pretty simple in terms of features, but it's a simple way of getting wired audio from your Switch (or any other console).

This gaming headset is roughly a year old, so is starting to see discounts. It gives you an affordable way to experience some of Turtle Beach's popular audio features, and it's pretty lightweight compared to rivals too.

HyperX offers a fair few gaming headsets we recommend, but thanks to the discount, this is perhaps the cheapest. It's surprisingly cheap when you consider it has dual drivers, offering sonic nuance many alternatives miss.

Coming just under the £50 threshold is this alternative HyperX model, which has a wider range of connection options than the above model and has a more durable frame. It's also designed to be comfortable with soft leatherette padding and memory foam cushions.

The main appeal of almost any gaming headset is thus: dedicated cans will sound better than the tinny loudspeakers you get in a handheld console. The presence of a proper microphone is a benefit too, if you play online with people.

If you usually play your Switch 2 on your home TV, while it's docked, you might not therefore need a gaming headset. Maybe your TV's built-in speakers, or the loudspeakers or soundbar you use for it, work just as well.

I'd therefore recommend a headset mostly to people who play their Switch 2 on the go. In many situations, you can't play your Switch out loud in the first place, so a headset is important, especially since all cans block out surrounding noise by virtue of their padded ear cushions.

But what about cheap versus expensive headsets? Honestly, I think pricey cans are best suited to competitive esports players who need to hear everything around them, or PC gamers who'll have much better access to the headphone software. Usually, what you're paying for is an elite roster of tools, features and preset EQ modes, and it's often hard to play around with those tools if you're not on a computer.

So for most buyers, a budget pair of cans like this is perfect, because audio quality is often the one thing you're not compromising on. The only thing you might want, that costs more, is a wireless connection. If you don't like the idea of using a physical cable, maybe you should pay a little bit more, but convenience is the only benefit to a Bluetooth connection in gaming headsets.

#3748. EA is resurrecting a dead commentator with AI for EA Sports FC 27, years after his last appearance in a FIFA game

"He was the very first voice of our game - so we really wanted to do him justice and bring him back."

EA Sports FC 27 is using gen-AI to digitally recreate the voice of veteran football commentator John Motson - the FIFA video game series' first ever real-world announcer who died in 2023.

John Motson commentated on hundreds of football games over the course of five different decades, starting in the 1970s. The English commentator then became the mainstay voice of EA's dominant football simulation series, beginning with FIFA 96 all the way up until FIFA 2005, when the publisher decided to go in a different direction.

But EA's now decided to digitally resurrect Motson - or, at least, his incredibly recognisable voice - with permission from his family. An update with Motson's voice will go live on 26th November. "There was no way we would have moved forward with this in any way, shape or form if they weren't fully on board," senior game designer director Mat Prior said in a statement given to the BBC earlier today.

"At the outset we wanted to pay tribute to to Motty as the commentator and as this emotional connection - he was the very first voice of our game - so we really wanted to do him justice and bring him back," Prior added, explaining that Motson's posthumous role in the game is being handled with a mixture of previously recorded voice lines and AI. EA supposedly went down the AI route since it doesn't have recordings of Motson commentating over newer, more fresh faced footballers.

Fred Motson said it "means an awful lot" to hear his dad's voice in the game again, and he reckons his dad was "always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects," even if he wasn't the most technologically savvy person. EA said it had paid the family for the rights to use Motson's voice and likeness.

Save Our Voices Now founder Peter Caulfield - who campaigns for the government to regulate the use of generative AI voice cloning tech - told the BBC he wasn't comfortable with the project. "In life or in death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed," he said. "Being a family member shouldn't automatically give you that right either." He doesn't have a problem with actors consenting to AI voice replication while they're still alive, however.

A Japanese acting union recently fought back against this very same practice by proposing new guidelines that would stop the replication of dead actors' voices without their permission.

Generative AI has been widely controversial in the games industry for other reasons, too. In recent months, there's been a huge impact on smaller game developers who are worried that their games could be cloned by AI copycats and some who have had to delay their release dates because of Steam's growing approvals backlog.

"The Grounds comes across as a frippery, Ultimate Team rumbles ever on, but FC 27 brings meaningful changes to the fluidity and speed of play. Given that its practical football-game monopoly is more or less unchallenged, EA could do a lot less than this," Josh Wise wrote in Eurogamer's EA Sports FC 27 review.

#3747. "This isn't a sign to retreat": Rockstar's historic union vote has failed, with 75% voting against, but the organisers are going to "keep fighting"

Rockstar touts "direct relationships" with staff

The potentially historic vote at GTA 6 creators Rockstar Games on whether to seek formal union recognition has failed, the International Workers of Great Britain have announced. Around 1600 studio members cast ballots across 12th to 26th November, even as the company's open world Bonnie & Clyde 'em up released onto PlayStation and Xbox storefronts. In the end, approximately 25% of the participants voted in favour.

According to the IWGB themselves, "the result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organising with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives."

Speaking to RPS in an emailed statement, Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe argued that the vote's failure "reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong." The IWGB, meanwhile, have declared that "this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for". They're going to keep mobilising for more labour power, with the failed vote now framed as a foot in the door.

"Whilst we haven't emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening," reads the union statement. "People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We head from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions will lead us.

"A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy," they continue. "But it's one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We'll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs."

The Rockstar UK unionisation drive has been a long journey. The vote follows open confrontation between Rockstar management in the UK and IWGB-affiliated Rockstar employees working out of a private Discord server. After allegedly keeping the Discord server under surveillance for over two years, Rockstar bosses fired around 30 staff in October 2026 on charges of "gross misconduct" and breach of confidentiality. The IWGB and the fired workers have countered by accusing Rockstar of union-busting, observing that the Discord's putative union membership had reached the 10% minimum required for statutory recognition under UK law, shortly before the firings.

220 Rockstar staff subsequently signed an open letter to management calling for the reinstatement of the fired workers. The IWGB also organised protest rallies outside the offices of Rockstar North in Edinburgh and Take-Two Interactive in London. A UK Member of Parliament weighed in, calling on ministers to "stop this from happening again". Finally, the ousted workers took Rockstar to court in an employment tribunal that has run for much of this year: the closing statements landed on the eve of GTA 6's release, with a judge's verdict pending.

I'm sorry to see the union vote fall through, given the boost a formally recognised GTA developer union in the UK would have given to labour organisation across the industry. In the short term, of course, it might have made for a safer and more supportive workplace at Rockstar. While there is relatively little recent reporting on current working conditions, many Rockstar games are allegedly the product of "crunch culture", stemming back to the development of the first 3D Grand Theft Autos on PS2.

In January 2010, an anonymous user posting on behalf of the “wives of Rockstar San Diego employees" claimed that staff had been forced to work 12-hour, six day weeks to finish the first Red Dead Redemption. A landmark report from Kotaku in 2018, based on interviews with 34 current and 43 former employees, described developers piling up evening and weekend work across Rockstar's empire, with crunch especially severe among QA staff at Rockstar Lincoln in the UK.

Some of Kotaku's sources said they had been explicitly pushed to work overtime by managers, facilitated by workplace systems such as hour-logging. Others spoke of a more vaporous expectation that they put in inhuman effort, because after all, working at the studio behind GTA is a privilege. Many had fond memories of their experiences, even as they acknowledged the toll taken on their minds, bodies and relationships outside work. This is part of the problem with crunch - it doesn't have to be explicitly imposed. It comes about because some creative and enthusiastic people are not good at recognising their own limits, and less scrupulous employers are happy to profit from this and, worse, erect a working culture around it.

The 2018 Kotaku piece acknowledges that some crunch results from the uneven and unpredictable way many videogames are made, but it also talks about overtime brought on by unaccountable leadership, with studio co-founders Dan and Sam Houser "renowned for rebooting, overhauling, and discarding large chunks of their games." (Dan Houser left the company in 2020.) The same heads were also said to value the "appearance" of developers going the extra mile, with one dev telling the site they were encouraged to walk a lap of the office on Saturday, whenever the Housers were in town. Together with anxieties about confidentiality, that emphasis on devs being visibly busy perhaps informs Rockstar's cancelling of hybrid working in early 2024, which precipitated some of this year's union activism.

Many of the people pushing for unionisation at Rockstar are also reacting to events across the games industry. There has been a huge wave of mass layoffs as companies "adjust" following the boom period initiated by Covid lockdowns. Some of those laid off had recently shipped commercially successful games, like Battlefield 6. GTA 6 developers have publicly expressed concerns about getting cut, even as their new open worlder makes sales records.

A chunk of the recent mass layoffs are owing to lucrative company acquisitions and consolidations that have attracted criticism from existing unions. Microsoft have spent two years axing studios, projects and jobs after spending around $69 billion to acquire Activision Blizzard. EA are now owned by a consortium led by Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund and Donald Trump's son-in-law; the company has since laid off hundreds of developers and closed the mighty BioWare as they shoulder an enormous debt, which they're reportedly hoping to offset by means of mass generative AI-powered costcutting. As alluded to in today's IWGB statement, there is the overarching question of how genAI - often explicitly mandated by executives - will threaten livelihoods by automating tasks, giving bosses an excuse to keep headcounts small by one means or another.

The repeated layoff waves have inspired a lot of union action at many large videogame companies, from Microsoft to Ubisoft, but I suspect a lot of that hasn't been apparent outside labour organising and enthusiast circles. GTA is as breakthrough a vidya as you can get. Rockstar forming a union would have been a foundation from which to talk more about worker power beyond the games industry.

As often when reporting on unionisation, I'm left idly wondering about what kind of art a fully unionised industry would create. The production conditions of many games can be deduced from their design – a photorealistic open world game, for example, is a vast assemblage of resources that may hinge on distributed development across an unequal world. Rockstar both represent AAA gaming at its grAAAndest, and have historically been part of the auteur craze, with the Housers having the final say on every detail.

We are, in general, all very familiar with the caricatures of auteur-led development, positioned as a source of both eccentric brilliance and ruinous hubris. I think there's much less of a narrative for the kind of art you get from teams where workers have serious negotiating power, though there are precedents in the form of cooperatives and similar organisations that tether their labour conditions more boldly to the kind of art they produce: for example, Die Gute Fabrik, and most recently, Summer Eternal.

A unionised Rockstar wouldn't just be a space in which workers are better protected against the expectations of managers and financial stakeholders; you'd get different kinds of art. Maybe more interesting kinds of art! I do wonder if union organisers could do a more effective job of expressing this hope, perhaps exploring where certain games have lost their way because workers were treated like cannon fodder.

Grabbing a Truffade Thrax in GTA 6 isn't too hard, but if you want Andrew Node's supercharged version, the true fastest car around, you'll need to complete a little collectible hunt. Before you start, it's worth noting that this special Truffade Thrax costs 70k to register when you steal it, though you can also sell it to Randy for 20k (not that I would recommend this as it's a unique car).

The first step is scanning ten No Flusher toilet graffiti stamps around Vice Beach, the east portion of Vice City, with your WAiNK It app. Each symbol is basically a little blue toilet. After that, you'll have to head to a secret lockup, and then you're on for stealing the car.

This first one is southeast of Nola - Ocean beach on the pavement on the west side of the road.

The second is east of Podium Sports - Ocean Beach, on the south side pavement of the road leading out onto the grass towards the beach.

This one is at the east end of the bridge leading from Vice Beach to Waxman Island, on the southern pavement. Also to the west of LTD Gas - Ocean Beach

This fourth one is east of Aural Expert and north of Venus Fitness, on the pavement at the side of the junction.

This one is on the pavement directly in front of Banana Hole Main Bar, east down the road from the previous one above.

This sixth one is on the sidewalk on the far west of the road running along the bottom of the huge park in Vice Beach.

This seventh is west of Podium Sports - Ocean Beach, down the road you can see with the roundabout at the end on the map.

The eighth is east down the road from Shorefront - Ocean Beach bank and south of Easy Electronics, on the pavement on the corner.

This ninth is north of Marshal's jewelry and northeast of Endzone - Washington Beach, at the east end of the big carpark bordering the beach.

On the right side of the northern road at the Oldby Island junction, directly opposite Ron Gas - Washington Beach.

After you've found all ten, Cal's conspiracy theory chat (which unlocks after the first) will go dark, before you get a separate message a little later giving you their hideout location. Head there, read the note to the right of the garage door, and then look on the back of it to get the code for the lock:

Inside you'll have a bunch of evidence pointing to Andrew Node's house on Starfish island, so examine it all and then you're ready to steal the car.

First off, Starfish Island is a gated community with security, so it's better to get a boat there. Head west from the hideout and steal a boat on the piers, then drive west across the water to the jetty of Andrew Node's house—it's the one on the southern side towards the centre, that looks like a backwards L.

Dock, head around the left side of the house to find a white garage on the right you can open up with Andrew Node's Truffade Thrax inside. You'll have to drive it off the island, but after that you can head to Randy and register it for 70k. Just make sure you have the garage space and the money before you steal the car.

#3745. The Witcher 3 Remastered's latest patch takes aim at mods nicking all of Geralt's possessions, disappearing buildings and an outbreak of "overly bright red" NPC leg areas

Catronia's not the only plague the Northern Realms need fear, it seems

The Witcher 3 Remastered continues to recieve tweaks ahead of the Songs of the Past expansion arriving next year to whisk Gerry from the River off on a fresh adventure. Following some bloomin' improvements in October, its latest patch does a bunch of skill and mutation balancing, alongside further technical tweaks and fixes for some funky bugs.

"Fixed an issue where Reforging the Mastercrafted or Grandmaster Feline armor gave Geralt an unusual hairstyle," reads the first of numerous notes in the visual section of patch 5.02's notes about weird stuff happening to Gerry's luscious mane. "Fixed an issue where Geralt could become bald after enabling HairWorks on PC or Xbox Play Anywhere and then continuing the game on Xbox via Cross Progression," reads another that sounds slightly more serious. "Fixed an issue where growing a beard with the Rabble-rouser hairstyle made Geralt's head invisible," reads a third, which takes the cake.

There've also been instances of Gerry or NPCs missing their faces or "other body parts". The NPCs, bless them, have also had to deal with contracting "overly bright red areas on their legs" when moving through crowds. Oh, and a building near Novigrad's docks has been cheeklily disappearing whenever Geralt gets close to it. One would assume it's just a bit shy, though that's a tough thing to be when your location means people embarking and disembarking from ships are constantly walking past. To be honest, it also sounds like it could have been adapted into an extra contract for Gerry if CD Projekt had fancied. The studio have also "fixed an issue where installing and uninstalling mods could cause merchants' inventories, Geralt's inventory and storage to be emptied".

Beyond the giggle-worthy bug fixes, the most consequential aspect of the patch to my eye will likely be the tweaks to the power of certain skills and mutations, which folks may well be testing out if they're trying to settle on a new build before Songs of the Past. Those tweaks are as follows:

Generally speaking, sign-heavy Gerry builds look like they'll be most acutely affected and be less effective following this patch. I typically only rely on Quen for a bit of shielding, because I'm an unimaginative monster slayer, so I'm not sure I'll notice it too much, but if you really make the most of your magical abilities it might hit your Gerry pretty hard.

It's worth skimming through the full notes if you've time, which also contain a few PC-specific fixes and tweaks. Starting a Hearts of Stone or Blood and Wine-only playthrough on Steam Deck should no longer lead to long load times, for example, while there've been some improvements made to path tracing and ray reconstruction .

#3744. Original Devil May Cry and Bayonetta director Hideki Kamiya really wants Konami to let him make a "truly insane" Castlevania game

Action game maestro Hideki Kamiya really wants to make a new Castlevania game with publisher Konami.

The long-time developer best known for his work in the director's chair on a host of beloved games - Bayonetta, Resident Evil 2, Okami, Devil May Cry and The Wonderful 101 included - recently published a new video to his personal YouTube account. While the video was first recorded last year, it does give us some hints on what Kamiya is interested in making after his in-development Okami sequel wraps up.

Perhaps the most noteworthy tidbit came from Kamiya advocating to make a new game in Konami's vampiric action-adventure series. "We'll definitely make Castlevania. If you let us work on it, we can make something truly insane, so just contact us and we'll be at your service," Kamiya said. (Thanks, Automaton!)

Kamiya presumably has his hands full with Capcom's Okami 2, which is currently in production at the director's newfound independent studio Clovers. Needless to say, any potential Kamiya-led Castlevania game will likely need to wait in a coffin for a while more.

In the meantime, it's not like Castlevania has remained dormant and defanged. Earlier this year, Konami promised that "numerous new products around Castlevania" are in the pipeline. While new games weren't explicitly confirmed, it's safe to assume Konami would be interested in hearing pitches from outside devs. Kamiya can stay hopeful knowing that Evil Empire just dropped another gorgeous, aggressive action-platformer in the series.

"Like Rose herself, the game is earnest, intelligent, and capable of brilliance. But, mimicking its protagonist, it is also awkward, and unable to fully come to terms with its own unique identity in the shadow of its over-bearing legacy," Dom wrote in Eurogamer's Castlevania: Belmont's Curse review. "By no means is Belmont's Curse a bad game, I just think Evil Empire sunk its teeth a bit too deep into something it wasn't quite ready to consume."

This isn't the first time Kamiya has publicly expressed interest in reviving older games, either. He recently said he's "100% serious" about bringing back Scalebound, his cancelled Xbox One exclusive.

Analyst estimates have put GTA 6 at 53 million copies sold, which, if accurate, places it as the 13th best-selling game of all time after just a week.

In the least surprising bit of news of 2026, GTA 6 is selling pretty well. It was probably the most anticipated game ever and is the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic, so naturally the sales have followed. The first official number from Rockstar Games placed it at 32.5 million copies sold before it was even released, which had made it the 30th best-selling game ever above the likes of Super Mario Odyssey, Monster Hunter World, and Elden Ring. But that was just pre-release, so it's no shock to say that its fortunes haven't ended there.

Alinea Analytics' head of market analysis, Rhys Elliott, posts the latest estimate over on Twitter, which places Rockstar's latest at 53 million copies sold, making $4.7 billion in its first week.

If this number is accurate, GTA 6 is the 13th best-selling game ever, with it unseating Animal Crossing: New Horizons, and overtaking the likes of Cyberpunk 2077, The Sims, and the Pokemon Generation 1 games (which have a combined sales figure of 47.44 million across Red, Blue and Yellow).

GTA 6 has sold 53M copies (75.7% on PS5) after a week on the market (@alineaanalytics estimates). Some other quick stats from our estimates: - It's made $4.7B (76.1% on PS5, due to regional prices) - 7M players have already played for over 50 hours. - 250K folks have played for over 100 hours (!!!!) - The US accounts for 33.5% of PS5's GTA 6 copies. Publishing another big deep dive on Substack shortly.November 27, 2026

Elliott's data also estimates that just under a quarter of GTA 6 sales were on Xbox, with the Series X|S version accounting for 13 million vs PS5's 40 million. And it's not like it's just selling well either, as he reckons that seven million players have already played over 50 hours, with 250k of those having already played 100 hours. For reference, the game had been out in New Zealand around 219 hours at the time the tweet was posted.

Obviously, this is massively impressive no matter how you look at it. But it's worth keeping in mind that the PC release hasn't even dropped yet, so this has the potential to skyrocket once more when PC players – and console players who are going to double dip – get their hands on it.

Playing Rockstar's new game? Be sure to read through our GTA 6 review and look through our GTA 6 guide for some more knowledge on the 2026 behemoth.

Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True was filmed at Disney World and mostly at night. Yes, this new Hallmark movie was filmed at Disney World and at night. So, while the experience was magical, the cast and crew of this project on the 2026 Christmas movie schedule kind of had to turn into vampires to survive. With that in mind, I had to ask the movie’s star, Lacey Chabert, and her colleagues what exactly it was like to film in the most magical place on Earth during the hours of the day when most people are fast asleep.

While working in the parks after hours must have been an exciting prospect for the cast of Holiday Ever After, in practice it took a bit to get used to it. They were working through the night instead of the day, and according to Philip actor Travis Van Winkle, it took a second to adjust to that:

It takes a second for your whole body to adjust to that, but once you do, you become a vampire. And it's kind of nice being awake at four in the morning, and you're just wide awake, and you know, excited to film a scene. And then to watch the sunrise every morning at Disney World when no one's in the park. I mean, it was very surreal that happened every night, every morning.

Sam actor Bryce Durfee and producer David Wulf also brought up how they kind of felt like vampires making this movie. Durfee specifically said that staying awake sometimes was legitimately hard, and that is what led to this back-and-forth:

Executive producer Jennifer Aspen made it very clear that what these actors pulled off with these night shoots was “pretty exceptional.” That’s because, not only were they working on vampire hours, they also had to make sure everything got done before the sun came up and the crowds came in.

To that point, Wulf said that behind the scenes they were “communicating with every element of the parks” to make sure they got the most “amazing moment for Hallmark” without “interfering with the guest experience.” Meanwhile, while they were capturing all of that, the cast also got to experience the magic of Disney World.

Thankfully, the cast aren’t really vampires, and they could see the sunrise each morning on set (which, again, was Disney World). Lacey Chabert, who plays Lindsey in the movie, told me that was her favorite part of these night shoots too. After saying the parks were “magical” during that time, she also said:

My favorite moment was when we would finish our night shoot, then we would shoot some daytime things early in the morning, seeing the park open. The music starts. They make an announcement. Rope drop happens. People run in, and it's just this infectious excitement and joy. And I hope that all of that comes through the movie. I know that it does.

The Mean Girls actress also explained that those magical feelings were there as they were getting ready for their night shoots, too. That’s because, as they were getting ready, the parks were preparing to close, and Magic Kingdom’s fireworks would be happening:

Yeah, and our base camp was in the parking lot of Magic Kingdom, and usually our call time was about 9 o'clock, so we could watch the fireworks from the makeup trailer. I mean, once in a lifetime.

Actors get to have surreal filming experiences all the time. However, getting ready while the fireworks go off is seriously iconic.

Taegen Burns (she plays Kiera) also used the word “magical” to describe this whole experience too. She explained that despite the “wonky hours,” getting to be in the parks without other people was “incredible.”

So, now that I’ve quoted so many positive adjectives the cast used, it’s clear that feeling like vampires while filming this entry on the 2026 TV schedule didn’t bother them much. And if it did, the magical nature of being at Disney World made up for it.

Now, to see what they made during the wee hours of the night in the most magical place on earth, you can catch Holiday Every After on the Hallmark Channel on Saturday, November 28 at 8 p.m. ET, and you can stream it the next day on Hallmark+ or with a Hulu or Disney+ subscription.

#3741. The Fable reboot had to look beyond Lionhead's RPG trilogy because games like The Witcher 3 "became the gold standard"

Developer Playground Games had to look beyond Lionhead's original run of Fable games when rebooting the classic fantasy series, and it's all thanks to games like The Witcher 3, which changed what many players expect from their big RPGs and set a new "gold standard."

The upcoming Fable reboot is finally ending its decade-long development journey soon. Playground Games had to set up an entirely new team to work on its fairytale revival, so Fable's production wasn't quite as smooth sailing as the studio's consistently excellent Forza Horizon series, for example.

Asked about what's changed during that time, in an interview with GamesIndustry.biz, studio founder and general manager Ralph Fulton named technological advancements as a biggie, but the impact of other games was perhaps even greater.

"In 2015, The Witcher 3 redefined what an open-world action RPG looks like and became the gold standard," Fulton said. "And after that bar was raised, the Assassin's Creed franchise changed into this more modern iteration with Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla, and became like a quasi-RPG."

"All of these games continue to reset player expectations," he continued. Millions of players suddenly had certain expectations about what their big-budget, open-world role-playing games should look like. So, Playground couldn't pull inspiration from Fable and Fable alone.

"I think looking only to the original Fable trilogy for inspiration would leave us lacking in terms of what the modern audience, the modern marketplace, expects," Fulton added.

Still, Playground's Fable is drawing most heavily from Lionhead's Fable. Fulton specifically mentions the game's signature British wit and in-flux morality system as examples. Then there's also the spontaneous life sim elements that "none of our competitors do," according to Fulton. "It's a totally Fable thing, the social simulation and economic simulation. Okay, there are games that have economic simulations, but they're not in [our] RPG category. Fable is unique in that it's almost like a life sim in terms of genre."

Raising four separate families and becoming the entire map's benevolent landlord was one of the funnest parts of Fable back in the day, alongside those sometimes silly characters. Seeing next year's Fable lean into those systemic choices, and having Albion's NPCs react to them more believably, could give this one a very long shelf life.

#3740. Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2's latest updates introduces a Weekly Clash mode that shakes up PvP with some constricting modifiers

In as booming a monster truck rally commentator voice as you can imagine: ARE YOU READY TO GET DECIMATED??? Yes? Yippee! Because I've got some good news for you. The latest update for Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 is here, appropriately dubbed the Decimation update, which adds in a new mode and more.

First up, that new mode! It's called Weekly Clash and it's for the competitive folks out there. "This new PvP shakes things up with the introduction of “Weekly Clash”, a new mode that brings unique new rules to Eternal War, like games restricted to a single class, a single weapon or even granting near-unlimited grenades," explains a Steam blog post. "Except more modifiers to be added in the future."

This update also introduces a new Chaos Siege sector, that new mode introduced last month, which adds in a "new playable sector bringing a renewed challenge between waves 11 and 15!" You'll also find six new heroic weapons in the armoury, like the omnissian axe, plasma incinerator and heavy bolter. This comes complete with some new heroic armour pieces, specifically four new helmets. On top of all of this, there's been a Vanguard rework: "Fight the enemies of Humanity with new ways to use your Grapnel Launcher! Attack cancellations, close-quarter kicks and a new Revenge mechanic make the Vanguard as bold and brutal as he’s ever been!"

Some other general tweaks have been made with this patch too. All PvP maps have seen the number and locations of ammo and equipment pickups adjusted, and conditions for the spawn position swap system have been improved. A level lock for the Absolute Siege and Absolute Stratagems mode has also been added; "The difficulty will be accessible to Classes that have reached level 25 or achieved Prestige at least once." And you'll also find that loading times and general connectivity should be a bit better!

The Bravado Banshee is another one of the cars you'll need to track down for Randy in GTA 6, but unlike the Pegassi Infernus, this one doesn't involve anything as dodgy as robbing a police lockup.

You can find this car inside the Sunrise Premium Autos showroom at the north tip of Southside, southwest of Pay 'N' Spray - Salton or east across the road from Ron Gas - Southside. This region is to the northeast of Hamlet.

There are two showrooms here, so make sure you have the right one, though the other does contain Pfister Growlers, in case you haven't gotten that car for Randy yet, either. Head inside to find the car—if you've played previous GTAs, you'll recognise it as a convertible with a white stripe down the middle. Hop inside, use the key cloner, and drive it through the glass.

This might damage it a bit, but you can always repair it at Ron Gas nearby, or at the gas station near Randy's shop. Just remember to drive fast, and if the tracker starts to beep, speed up to stop it pinging your location to the cops. Delivering this one gets you 6,500k and a 5k condition bonus as usual if it's in good nick.

#3738. GTA 6 reinvigorates PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X console sales in the US, even at their inflated prices

Despite the far higher prices of PlayStation and Xbox consoles today compared to their launch, or even the same period last year, both brands of console saw a significant boost in US sales leading up to the launch of this generation's biggest game: Grand Theft Auto 6.

In the week ending 14th November, PS5 hardware unit sales registered a 2.4x increase over the same week last year. Xbox wasn't far behind, seeing a 2.3x increase in its own unit sales. That's according to industry analyst Mat Piscatella at Circana, who pulled the data from Circana's retail tracking service, which covers the US retail market.

The PS5 Pro only accounted for less than 10 percent of the PlayStation's total unit sales, by the way, which Piscatella noted was "a LOT better than it has been in recent weeks", and seemingly the result of increased supply.

GTA 6, of course, released on 19th November, so the surge in console hardware sales was clearly driven by the rush to attain consoles before the game came out. And while the GTA 6-driven demand isn't surprising, it's worth noting how much more expensive PS5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles are today.

A standard PS5 today costs $650, compared to $550 a year ago. The PS5 Pro saw a big jump from $750 last November to $900 today. The base Xbox Series X jumped from $650 last year to $800 today, while Series S now costs $500, up from $400.

Even Switch 2, where GTA 6 is not available, saw a notable boost of 40 percent in hardware sales over the same period, driven by The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and the special edition Zelda Switch 2 console.

Circana's November US video game market report, which releases in December, is already one of the most anticipated this year, for digesting and documenting the GTA 6 effect. Worldwide, GTA 6 sold more than 32.5m copies in one day, making Rockstar's parent company Take-Two $3.79bn (£2.89bn) in revenue. We haven't had any updated official sales figures since; but estimates suggest the sales figure could be well into the 40-millions. Perhaps Rockstar is waiting to hit the nice round 50m sales mark before announcing it.

If you're playing GTA 6, you may want to keep Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough to hand. It has plenty of very helpful guides covering the game's main missions, as well as explainers for mechanics like romance and the criminal profile, and even cheats for when you finish the game.

#3737. HARK THE GHOUL is a Victorian gothic dungeon crawler RPG that features a trench-coat-wearing rat man who wants to sell you rats a la counterfeit watches

I'm a simple person. I see an anthropomorphic rat man who opens up his trench coat that is filled with regular rats in the same manner as one would with counterfeit watches in a trailer for a video game, I add it to my wishlist. There really isn't much I need in life, but that certainly fulfills those needs. And it's exactly what HARK THE GHOUL is offering, an action-adventure, dungeon crawler RPG set in a weird and nasty Victorian gothic city with an emphasis on free exploration.

Now, I appreciate not all of you will be as immediately convinced by trench coat wearing rat men, so let's have a deeper gander at the game together. Exploration really does seem to be the key thing here, not just in terms of going wherever you want, more or less when you want, but how you get about. For example, say there's an annoying gap you want to cross. Use a magical spell to summon a crate, then lob it in front of you, and cast some icey magic to freeze it into place, thereby creating a new platform for you to hop onto. Looks like nice and systemic stuff!

HARK THE GHOUL releases 👉JANUARY 21st, 2027!!!👈 Our action-adventure RPG built around freeform exploration lets you loose in a dark Victorian city full of secrets to uncover and ravenous monsters to defeat! Coming to Steam, Switch 1, Switch 2, PS5 and Xbox Series![image or embed]

This extends to the combat, which faces you against odd automatons, infected foes and nasty beasties. You can perform quite silly tricks like using your shovel to dig up a rock and chuck that at a baddie, or you can use your magic to conjure up an explosive crate which you then kick at an enemy, blasting it with a shotgun. It appears to almost be an RPG by way of the immersive sim; there's no correct way to go about the game, only the way you find most fun. Though maybe that's dredging up the debate around what an immersive sim is…

Either way, I'm just tickled pink by HARK THE GHOUL, which also pits you as a mothman-type figure who's just emerged from their cocoon. Delightful! And it just got a release date too: January 21st, 2027. That's only a couple of months away, obviously, but if you can't wait that long then there's a demo you can check out on Steam. Or, you know, just throw it a wishlist! Offering it some support either way seems like a nice idea.
